verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              अथोपगम्य विदुरमपराह्णे जनार्दनः। पितृष्वसारं स पृथामभ्यगच्छदरिन्दमः ॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said After his visit to Vidura, Janardana, the subduer of enemies, went in the afternoon to Pritha, his mother's sister.

verses.sanskrit: सा दृष्ट्वा कृष्णमायान्तं प्रसन्नादित्यवर्चसम्। कण्ठे गृहीत्वा प्राक्रोशत् स्मरन्ती तनयान् पृथा ॥२॥
verses.english: Seeing Krishna approaching and effulgent like the radiant sun, Pritha clasped his neck with her arms and poured forth her loud lamentations, remembering her sons.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां सत्त्ववतां मध्ये गोविन्दं सहचारिणम्। चिरस्य दृष्ट्वा वार्ष्णेयं बाष्पमाहारयत् पृथा ॥३॥
verses.english: Seeing Govinda after a long time, the action of the Vrishni race, companion of her sons, endued with prowess, Pritha shed tears.

verses.sanskrit: साऽब्रवीत् कृष्णमासीनं कृतातिथ्यं युधां पतिम्। बाष्पगद्गदपूर्णेन मुखेन परिशुष्यता ॥४॥
verses.english: She said to Krishna, the best of warriors who had seated himself after receiving the rites of hospitality, with her face dried up with woe and in a voice choked up with tears.

verses.sanskrit: ये ते बाल्यात् प्रभृत्येव गुरुशुश्रूषणे रताः। परस्परस्य सुहृदः सम्मताः समचेतसः। निकृत्या भ्रंशिता राज्याज्जनार्हा निर्जनं गताः ॥५॥
verses.english: 'Those, who ever since their childhood are attached to the service of their elders, those who are endued with humility and those who are of similar hearts, were deprived of their kingdom by deceit and sent into exile, through they were desirous of remaining in the society of men.

verses.sanskrit: विनीतक्रोधहर्षाश्च ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः। त्यक्त्वा प्रियसुखे पार्था रुदतीमपहाय माम् ॥६॥
verses.english: They, who have brought under control wrath and joy, who are devoted to the Brahmanas, who are speakers of truth, those sons of mine abandoning their dear enjoyments and leaving behind them myself weeping for them.

verses.sanskrit: अहार्षुश्च वनं यान्तः समूलं हृदयं मम। अतदर्हा महात्मानः कथं केशव पाण्डवाः ॥७॥
verses.english: Have gone to the forest, rendering the very bottom of my heart. These large-souled sons of Pandu undeserving of these miserieshow did they, O Keshava.

verses.sanskrit: ऊषुर्महावने तात सिंह-व्याघ्र-गजाकुले। बाला विहीनाः पित्रा ते मया सततलालिताः ॥८॥
verses.english: Live in that great forest, O child, abandoning, as it was, in lions, tigers and elephants. Losing their father in their boyhood, they were even reared and brought up by myself.

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यन्तश्च पितरौ कथमूषुर्महावने। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैर्मृदङ्गैर्वेणुनिःस्वनैः ॥९॥
verses.english: Without seeing their parents, how did they live in the great forest? By the sounds of conches and drums and the music of flutes.

verses.sanskrit: पाण्डवाः समबोध्यन्त बाल्यात्प्रभृति केशव। ये स्म वारणशब्देन हयानां हेषितेन च ॥१०॥
verses.english: Were the Pandavas awakened from their sleep ever since their infancy, O Keshava; who again, were by the roar of elephants and neighing of horses and by the rattles of the wheels of the chariots awakened from sleep at home-also by the sound of conches and cymbals accompanied with the music of flutes and lyres; and whose praises were sung by the twice-born at the break of day in high sounding songs; and who worshipped the deserving Brahmanas with the raiment's, gems and jewels; who, worthy of respect, themselves were blessed and done homage to by the largesouled Brahmanas by laudatory hymns and worshipped as well. How could they, lying on soft blankets and skin of the Ranku deer in the best parts of the palace, be awakened by hearing the loud roar of animals in the great forest?

verses.sanskrit: रथनेमिनिनादैश्च व्यबोध्यन्त तदा गृहे। शङ्खभेरीनिनादेन वेणुवीणानुनादिना ॥११॥
पुण्याहघोषमिश्रेण पूज्यमाना द्विजातिभिः। वस्त्रै रत्नैरलङ्कारैः पूजयन्तो द्विजन्मनः ॥१२॥
गीर्भिर्मङ्गलयुक्ताभिर्ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम्। अर्चितैरर्चनार्हैश्च स्तुवद्भिरभिनन्दिताः ॥१३॥
प्रासादाग्रेष्वबोध्यन्त राङ्कवाजिनशायिनः। क्रूरं च निनदं श्रुत्वा श्वापदानां महावने ॥१४॥
न स्मोपयान्ति निद्रान्ते न तदर्हा जनार्दन। भेरी-मृदङ्गनिनदैः शङ्ख-वैणव-निःस्वनैः ॥१५॥
verses.english: It does not seem possible to me that they obtained sleep, though they did not at all deserve this, O Janardana, those who by the sound of cymbals and drums and the conches and flutes and by the sweet music of songs by woman, O slayer of Madhu, were awakened and praised by the prisoners and professional bards-how could they.

verses.sanskrit: स्त्रीणां गीतनिनादैश्च मधुरैर्मधुसूदन। बन्दि-मागध-सूतैश्च स्तुवद्भिर्बोधिताः कथम् ॥१६॥
महावनेष्वबोध्यन्त श्वापदानां रुतेन च। ह्रीमान् सत्यधृतिर्दान्तो भूतानामनुकम्पिता ॥१७॥
verses.english: In the great forest be awakened at the roar of animals? The one endowed with modesty, truth, patience, self-control and kindness to animals and who bringing his desire and malice under control walks on the path followed by the good, he was capable of bearing the heavy burden of the ancient sages of royal descentnamely Amvarisha, Mandhatta, Yayati, Nahusha, Bharata, Dilipa, Shibi, the son of Ushanara; he who followed good habits of life and conversant with virtue, of true prowess, he who endued with all the virtuous uses, the king of all the three worlds, viz., the virtuous-souled Ajatashatru of a pious complexion and having a complexion like that of gold, chief among the Kurus and among all in respect of virtue and those who shape their habits of life to the ways indicated in the holy book, who is of handsome appcarance and of long arms, how is that Yudhishthira, O Krishna?

verses.sanskrit: कामद्वेषौ वशे कृत्वा सतां वर्त्मानुवर्तते। अम्बरीषस्य मान्धातुर्ययातेर्नहुषस्य च ॥१८॥
भरतस्य दिलीपस्य शिबेरौशीनरस्य च। राजर्षीणां पुराणानां धुरं धत्ते दुरुद्वहाम् ॥१९॥
शीलवृत्तोपसम्पन्नो धर्मज्ञः सत्यसङ्गरः। राजा सर्वगुणोपेतस्त्रैलोक्यस्यापि यो भवेत् ॥२०॥
अजातशत्रुर्धर्मात्मा शुद्धजाम्बूनदप्रभः। श्रेष्ठः कुरुषु सर्वेषु धर्मतः श्रुतवृत्ततः। प्रियदर्शो दीर्घभुजः कथं कृष्ण युधिष्ठिरः ॥२१॥
यः स नागायुतप्राणो वातरंहा महाबलः। सामर्षः पाण्डवो नित्यं प्रियो भ्रातुः प्रियङ्करः ॥२२॥
verses.english: He who is of as great strength as ten thousand elephants and of speed equal to the wind, that is, one of great prowess and ever wrathful among the sons of Pandu, who ever does good to his dear brothers; who sicw Kichaka with his cousins, 0 slayer of Madhu and Krodhavasha and of Hidimba and of Vaka; who is in strength equal to Shakra and in prowess equal to the god of wind, who is in wrath equal to the great Shiva, namely Bhima, foremost among smiters, that chastiser of foes, that wrathful son of Pandu, who controlling his rage and strength and wrath, stays with his soul under restraint, under the rule of his brother, that great-souled one, that man of energy, that foremost among men, that one of immeasurable prowess, that Bhima in appearance, too, is terrible looking (i.e. justifies his name), O Janardana.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रियो दर्शो दर्शनं यस्य दर्शादिश्राद्धकर्म वा यस्य ॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: कीचकस्य तु सज्ञातेर्यो हन्ता मधुसूदन। शूरः क्रोधवशानां च हिडिम्बस्य बकस्य च ॥२३॥
verses.bhavadeepa: सामर्षत्वादेव पाण्डवः पाण्डुरेव पाण्डवः स्वार्थे तद्धितः । यद्वा पाण्डवः पाण्डुपुत्रः । ‘पाण्डुः कुन्तीपतौ सिते’ इति विश्वः ॥२२॥

verses.sanskrit: पराक्रमे शक्रसमो मातरिश्वसमो बले। महेश्वरसमः क्रोधे भीमः प्रहरतां वरः ॥२४॥
क्रोधं बलममर्षं च यो निधाय परंतपः। जितात्मा पाण्डवोऽमर्षी भ्रातुस्तिष्ठति शासने ॥२५॥
तेजोराशिं महात्मानं वरिष्ठममितौजसम्। भीमं प्रदर्शनेनापि भीमसेनं जनार्दनम् ॥२६॥
तं ममाचक्ष्व वार्ष्णेय कथमद्य वृकोदरः। आस्ते परिघबाहुः स मध्यमः पाण्डवो बली ॥२७॥
verses.english: Tell me, O scion of the Vrishni race, how Vrikodara is doing now, the one having macelike arms, that mighty second son of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनेनार्जुनो यः स कृष्ण बाहुसहस्रिणा। द्विबाहुः स्पर्धते नित्यमतीतेनापि केशव ॥२८॥
verses.english: That two armed Arjuna, O Krishna, who is ever proud of being superior to that Arjuna of ancient days, who had a thousand arms, who with one of his arms darts with violence five hundred arrows, that son of Pandu, who in the use of arrows is equal to the royal son of Kartavirya, equal in energy to Aditya, in selfcontrol equal to a great Rishi, in forbearance equal to the Earth and in prowess equal to the great Indra, that strength by which all kings, the descendants of Kuru, have acquired this large territory of great effulgence; whose strength of arms all the sons of Pandu respect, that son of Pandu, foremost among all the carwarriors, of true prowess; going to whose front no one returns with his life, he, O Achyuta, who is accustomed to victories over all creatures and himself being invincible; who is the refuge of the Pandu's and even of the godsbe your brother and your friend, how is he at present, that Dhananjaya?

verses.sanskrit: क्षिपत्येकेन वेगेन पञ्च बाणशतानि यः। इष्वस्त्रे सदृशो राज्ञः कार्तवीर्यस्य पाण्डवः ॥२९॥
तेजसाऽऽदित्यसदृशो महर्षिसदृशो दमे। क्षमया पृथिवीतुल्यो महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः ॥३०॥
आधिराज्यं महद्दीप्तं प्रथितं मधुसूदन। आहृतं येन वीर्येण कुरूणां सर्वराजसु ॥३१॥
यस्य बाहुबलं सर्वे पाण्डवाः पर्युपासते। स सर्वरथिनां श्रेष्ठः पाण्डवः सत्यविक्रमः ॥३२॥
यं गत्वाऽभिमुखः संख्ये न जीवन् कश्चिदाव्रजेत्। यो जेता सर्वभूतानामजेयो जिष्णुरच्युत ॥३३॥
योऽपाश्रयः पाण्डवानां देवानामिव वासवः। स ते भ्राता सखा चैव कथमद्य धनञ्जयः ॥३४॥
दयावान् सर्वभूतेषु ह्रीनिषेवो महास्त्रवित्। मृदुश्च सुकुमारश्च धार्मिकश्च प्रियश्च मे ॥३५॥
verses.english: The one who is kind to all creatures endued with modesty and having a large knowledge of the nature and use of weapons, mild, delicate, virtuous and beloved by me; that great bow-man and hero Sahadeva, that ornament of assemblies, that youth, O Krishna, who is skillful at both religious deeds and profitable from an earthly point of view and properly waiting on his brothers.

verses.sanskrit: सहदेवो महेष्वासः शूरः समिति शोभनः। भ्रातॄणां कृष्ण शुश्रूषुर्धर्मार्थकुशलो युवा ॥३६॥
सदैव सहदेवस्य भ्रातरो मधुसूदन। वृत्तं कल्याणवृत्तस्य पूजयन्ति महात्मनः ॥३७॥
verses.english: Those large-souled brothers of Sahadeva, O Krishna, ever respect the habits of life of Sahadeva, who follows a good course of life-Tell me, O scion of the Vrishni race, of that son of Madri, of that heroic and veteran warrior, Sahadeva, the chief of warriors, who used to wait on me.

verses.sanskrit: ज्येष्ठोपचायिनं वीरं सहदेवं युधां पतिम्। शुश्रूषुं मम वार्ष्णेय माद्रीपुत्रं प्रचक्ष्व मे ॥३८॥
सुकुमारो युवा शूरो दर्शनीयश्च पाण्डवः। भ्रातॄणां चैव सर्वेषां प्रियः प्राणो बहिश्चरः ॥३९॥
verses.english: That heroic and delicate youth, that son of Pandu, well worth a gaze, is the life itself to all his brothers, though he has a different body.

verses.sanskrit: चित्रयोधी च नकुलो महेष्वासो महाबलः। कच्चित्स कुशली कृष्ण वत्सो मम सुखैधितः ॥४०॥
verses.english: My son, that great bow-man, Nakula of great prowess, that veteran warrior, brought up in luxury, is he well, O Krishna?

verses.sanskrit: सुखोचितमदुःखार्हं सुकुमारं महारथम्। अपि जातु महाबाहो पश्येयं नकुलं पुनः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Shall I behold again this Nakula, O you with long arms, that great car-warrior, brought up in luxury, deserving of every happiness and undeserving of all woe.

verses.sanskrit: पक्ष्मसम्पातजे काले नकुलेन विनाकृता। न लभामि धृतिं वीर साऽद्य जीवामि पश्य माम् ॥४२॥
verses.english: Separated from Nakula even for the shortest period of time, taken up by a wink, I obtained no peace of mind, O hero, behold me that I am still alive.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वैः पुत्रैः प्रियतरा द्रौपदी मे जनार्दन। कुलीना रूपसम्पन्ना सर्वैः समुदिता गुणैः ॥४३॥
verses.english: O Janardana, Draupadi is dearer to me than all my sons. She comes of a noble family, endued with beauty and endowed with all virtues.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रलोकात् पतिलोकं वृण्वाना सत्यवादिनी। प्रियान् पुत्रान् परित्यज्य पाण्डवाननुरुध्यते ॥४४॥
verses.english: That speaker of truth preferred the company of her husbands to that of her sons and leaving behind her dear sons, she follows the sons of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: महाभिजनसम्पन्ना सर्वकामैः सुपूजिता। ईश्वरी सर्वकल्याणी द्रौपदी कथमच्युत ॥४५॥
verses.english: O Achyuta, how is the all blessed queen Draupadi of illustrious birth well gratified with the fulfillment of all her desires?
verses.bhavadeepa: पुत्रलोकात् पुत्रसन्निकर्षं त्यक्त्वा पतिलोकं पतिसन्निधिं वृण्वाना  ॥४४॥

verses.sanskrit: यतिभिः पञ्चभिः शूरैरग्निकल्पैः प्रहारिभिः। उपपन्ना महेष्वासैर्द्रौपदी दुःखभागिनी ॥४६॥
verses.english: Draupadi has a bad lot, though she has five husbands, all heroes like the fire, all smiters of foes and all great bowmen.

verses.sanskrit: चतुर्दशमिदं वर्षं यन्नापश्यमरिन्दम। पुत्रादिभिः परिद्यूनां द्रौपदीं सत्यवादिनीम् ॥४७॥
verses.english: O chastiser of foes, the one whom I have not seen for these fourteen years, that Draupadi, truthful of speech, is anxious for her children.

verses.sanskrit: न नूनं कर्मभिः पुण्यैरश्नुते पुरुषः सुखम्। द्रौपदी चेत्तथावृत्ता नाश्नुते सुखमव्ययम् ॥४८॥
verses.english: It seems that a man does not surely get happiness as the result of his virtuous acts; for Draupadi, though of virtuous habits of life, does not get unending happiness.

verses.sanskrit: न प्रियो मम कृष्णाया बीभत्सुर्न युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनो यमौ वाऽपि यदपश्यं सभागताम् ॥४९॥
verses.english: When I remember Krishna dragged to the Assembly-Hall, Vibhatsu, Yudhishthira, Bhimasena and also the twin brothers, Nakula and Sahadeva cease to be dear to me.

verses.sanskrit: न मे दुःखतरं किञ्चिद्भूतपूर्वं ततोऽधिकम्। स्त्रीधर्मिणीं द्रौपदीं यच्छ्वशुराणां समीपगाम् ॥५०॥
verses.english: Nothing ever before gave me greater pain than the dragging of Draupadi in her season to her father-in-law. was

verses.sanskrit: आनायितामनार्येण क्रोधलोभानुवर्तिना। सर्वे प्रेक्षन्त कुरव एकवस्त्रां सभागताम् ॥५१॥
verses.english: She dragged there by that dishonourable wretch, from motives of wrath and covetousness, and all the Kurus gazed on her brought to the Assembly-Hall in a single raiment.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रैव धृतराष्ट्रश्च महाराजश्च बाह्लिकः। कृपश्च सोमदत्तश्च निर्विण्णाः कुरवस्तथा ॥५२॥
verses.english: There were at the time Dhritarashtra, the great king Balhika, Kripa, Somadatta and the Kurus who were pained at it.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यां संसदि सर्वेषां क्षत्तारं पूजयाम्यहम्। वृत्तेन हि भवत्यार्यो न धनेन न विद्यया ॥५३॥
verses.english: Of all the people present in that assembly I honour that Kshatta (Vidura) most; for a man becomes honourable by his habits and not by his wealth, nor by his knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य कृष्ण महाबुद्धेर्गंभीरस्य महात्मनः। क्षत्तुः शीलमलङ्कारो लोकान्विष्टभ्य तिष्ठति ॥५४॥
verses.english: O Krishna, the virtues of that high-souled Kshatta of great and deep wisdom are like an ornament of the whole world.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              सा शोकार्ता च हृष्टा च दृष्ट्वा गोविन्दमागतम्। नानाविधानि दुःखानि सर्वाण्येवान्वकीर्तयत् ॥५५॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said That lady oppressed with sorrow and yet cheerful seeing Govinda come, began to describe all the diverse grief's she had suffered.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वैराचरितं यत्तत्कुराजभिररिन्दम। अक्षद्यूतं मृगवधः कच्चिदेषां सुखावहम् ॥५६॥
verses.english: O chastiser of foes, could game at dice and the slaying of deer practised by these bad kings in the days of old be pleasant to them?

verses.sanskrit: तन्मां दहति यत्कृष्णा सभायां कुरुसन्निधौ। धार्तराष्ट्रैः परिक्लिष्टा यथा नकुशलं तथा ॥५७॥
verses.english: The degree, to which this fact pains me, namely the dragging of Krishna to the Assembly-Hall in the presence of the Kurus and insulted by the sons of Dhritarashtra, is not equalled by death itself.
verses.bhavadeepa: कच्चिदिति काक्वा सुखावहत्वं नास्तीति व्यज्यते । एषां मत्पुत्रभर्त्रादीनाम् ॥५६॥

verses.sanskrit: निर्वासनं च नगरात् प्रव्रज्या च परंतप। नानाविधानां दुःखानामभिज्ञाऽस्मि जनार्दन ॥५८॥
verses.english: O chastiser of foes, the exile (of my sons) out of city and their wanderings and several other grief's have l experienced, O Janardana.

verses.sanskrit: अज्ञातचर्या बालानामवरोधश्च माधव। न मे क्लेशतमं तत्स्यात् पुत्रैः सह परंतप ॥५९॥
verses.english: O Madhava, O chastiser of foes, living in concealment and the deprivation of my boys, could not be so painful to me in the company of my sons?

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनेन निकृता वर्षमद्य चतुर्दशम्। दुःखादपि सुखं नः स्याद्यदि पुण्यफलक्षयः ॥६०॥
verses.english: It is fourteen years now since they were exiled by Duryodhana; and happiness should be ours, if misery puts an end to the fruits of vice.

verses.sanskrit: न मे विशेषो जात्वासीत् धार्तराष्ट्रेषु पाण्डवैः। तेन सत्येन कृष्ण त्वां हतामित्रं श्रिया वृतम्। अस्माद्विमुक्तं सङ्ग्रामात् पश्येयं पाण्डवैः सह ॥६१॥
verses.english: I never treated the sons of Dhritarashtra in a different way from that in which I treated the sons of Pandu; and by virtue of this truth shall I see, O Krishna, yourself along with the Pandavas after you have slain your enemies invested with prosperity, come out safe from this impending war.
verses.bhavadeepa: यदि सुखं पुण्यक्षयरूपम् । अर्थाद्दुःखं पापक्षयरूपं तर्हि दुःखात् पापक्षयहेतोस्तत्सुखं नः अस्माकं स्यात् । तथा च न वयं दुःखाद्भयं प्राप्नुम इत्यर्थः ॥६०॥

verses.sanskrit: नैव शक्याः पराजेतुं सर्वं ह्येषां तथाविधम्। पितरं त्वेव गर्हेयं नात्मानं न सुयोधनम् ॥६२॥
verses.english: All of them having such like qualities are incapable of being defeated by the enemies. But my father is to blame ((for all this grief) and not myself, nor Suyodhana.
verses.bhavadeepa: अस्मात् भाविनः कुरुपाण्डवसंग्रामात् गोत्रकलहे विषमधियामेवावमर्दः समबुद्धीनां तु सुखमेवेति भावः ॥६१॥

verses.sanskrit: येनाहं कुन्तिभोजाय धनं वृत्तैरिवार्पिता। बालां मामार्यकस्तुभ्यं क्रीडन्तीं कन्दुहस्तिकाम् ॥६३॥
verses.english: By him I was given away to Kuntibhoja like wealth given away by a rich man. While yet a girl playing with a ball in my hand, your grand-father.

verses.sanskrit: अदात्तु कुन्तिभोजाय सखा सख्ये महात्मने। साऽहं पित्रा च निकृता श्वशुरैश्च परंतप। अत्यन्तदुःखिता कृष्णा किं जीवितफलं मम ॥६४॥
verses.english: Gave me away to his friend, the largesouled Kuntibhoja; such a one was myself and abandoned by my father and my father-in-law. O chastiser of foes, meeting with great troubles, O Krishna, what is the use of my life?
verses.bhavadeepa: वृत्तैर्वदान्यत्वेन ख्यातैर्धनं यथा अक्लेशेनार्प्यते तद्वत् येनाहमर्पिता । ‘वृत्तोऽतीते दृढे ख्याते’ इति विश्वः । धूर्तैरिवेत्यपपाठः । आर्यकः पितामहः । तुभ्यं तव ॥६३॥

verses.sanskrit: यन्मां वागब्रवीन्नक्तं सूतके सव्यसाचिनः। पुत्रस्ते पृथिवीं जेता यशश्चास्य दिवं स्पृशेत् ॥६५॥
verses.english: At the birth of Savyasachi, a voice told me in the room in which I was confined-'Your son will be the conquer of the world and his fame will reach the very heaven.

verses.sanskrit: हत्वा कुरून् महाजन्ये राज्यं प्राप्य धनञ्जयः। भ्रातृभिः सह कौन्तेयस्त्रीन् मेधानाहरिष्यति ॥६६॥
verses.english: Slaughtering the Kurus in a great battle and obtaining the kingdom, Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, along with his brothers, will perform three grand sacrificial rites.'

verses.sanskrit: नाहं तामभ्यसूयामि नमो धर्माय वेधसे। कृष्णाय महते नित्यं धर्मो धारयति प्रजाः ॥६७॥
धर्मश्चेदस्ति वार्ष्णेय यथा वागभ्यभाषत। त्वं चापि तत्तथा कृष्ण सर्वं संपादयिष्यसि ॥६८॥
verses.english: If Dharma (Virtue) exists in this world, O scion of the Vrishni race, thus you too will be what the voice announced, O Krishna; and you will accomplish all that.
verses.bhavadeepa: अभ्यसूयामि निन्दामि वेधसे विश्वकर्त्रे महते इति कृष्णस्येश्वरस्य निन्दार्थमुपहासः । कर्मण एव प्राबल्यं धर्मपदस्यार्थदर्शनेनाह- धर्म इति । धारयतीति धर्म इति व्युत्पत्त्या धर्म एव कर्ता धारयिता । ईश्वराराधनं तु वृथैवेति भावः ॥६७॥

verses.sanskrit: न मां माधव वैधव्यं नार्थनाशो न वैरता। तथा शोकाय दहति यथा पुत्रैर्विनाभवः ॥६९॥
verses.english: O Madhava, neither widowhood, nor the loss of wealth, nor even this dispute has pained me so much as my separation from my sons.
verses.bhavadeepa: धर्मश्चेदिति । धर्मेऽपि संशयं दर्शयति सतोऽपीश्वरस्याकिञ्चित्करत्वमाह - त्वं चेति ॥६८॥

verses.sanskrit: याऽहं गाण्डीवधन्वानं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। धनञ्जयं न पश्यामि का शान्तिर्हृदयस्य मे। इतश्चतुर्दशं वर्षं यन्नापश्यं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥७०॥
verses.english: I, who do not see the wielder of the Gandiva bow, that foremost of all that wield weapons, Dhananjaya-what peace can I (my heart) know, not having seen Yudhishthira for these fourteen years?

verses.sanskrit: धनञ्जयं च गोविन्द यमौ तं च वृकोदरम्। जीवनाशं प्रनष्टानां श्राद्धं कुर्वन्ति मानवाः ॥७१॥
verses.english: Nor have I seen Dhananjaya, O Govinda, the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva and also that Vrikodara; people perform the Shradha (obsequies) of absent people under the impression that they are dead.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थतस्ते मम मृतास्तेषां चाहं जनार्दन। ब्रूया माधव राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥७२॥
verses.english: Virtually they are dead to me and I am the same to them, O Janardana, O Madhava, say this to the virtuous-souled king Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: भूयांस्ते हीयते धर्मो मा पुत्रक वृथा कृथाः। पराश्रया वासुदेव या जीवति धिगस्तु ताम् ॥७३॥
verses.english: To a mode of life attended with meanness death even is superior. Say also to Dhananjaya and Vrikodara who are constantly on the alert.

verses.sanskrit: वृत्तेः कार्पण्यलब्धाया अप्रतिष्ठैव ज्यायसी। अधो धनञ्जयं ब्रूया नित्योद्युक्तं वृकोदरम् ॥७४॥
verses.english: This is the time come for the purpose, for which a Kshatriya woman brings forth a son, if you let the occasion, which is now come, slip without doing anything;

verses.sanskrit: यदर्थं क्षत्रिया सूते तस्य कालोऽयमागतः। अस्मिंश्चेदागते काले मिथ्या चातिक्रमिष्यति ॥७५॥
लोकसंभाविताः सन्तः सुनृशंसं करिष्यथ। नृशंसेन च वो युक्तांस्त्यजेयं शाश्वतीः समाः ॥७६॥
verses.english: You will be doing what is cruel and mean, though you are respected by the world; and if you are ever contemptible, I shall abandon and disown you forever.

verses.sanskrit: काले हि समनुप्राप्ते त्यक्तव्यमपि जीवनम्। माद्रीपुत्रौ च वक्तव्यौ क्षत्रधर्मरतौ सदा ॥७७॥
verses.english: When the suitable moment arrives, life even should be laid down. The two sons of Madri who are ever attached to virtuous deeds should be spoken to.

verses.sanskrit: विक्रमेणार्जितान् भोगान् वृणीतं जीवितादपि। विक्रमाधिगता ह्यर्थाः क्षत्रधर्मेण जीवतः ॥७८॥
verses.english: Chose these comforts and luxuries, which are attainable by a display of your prowess, rather than even life itself, since objects attained by prowess alone are ever pleasing to those who live the life of Kshatriyas.

verses.sanskrit: मनो मनुष्यस्य सदा प्रीणन्ति पुरुषोत्तम। गत्वा ब्रूहि महाबाहो सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम् ॥७९॥
verses.english: And ever gladden the hearts of men, O you best among men. Having gone there speak to him who is the foremost among all wielders of weapons,

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनं पाण्डवं वीरं द्रौपद्याः पदवीं चर। विदितौ हि तवात्यन्तं क्रुद्धौ तौ तु यथान्तकौ ॥८०॥
verses.english: Namely the hero Arjuna, the son of Pandu. Follow the path pointed out by Draupadi. It is known to you that when they (Bhima and Arjuna) are enraged they are as Death himself.

verses.sanskrit: भीमार्जुनौ नयेतां हि देवानपि परां गतिम्। तयोश्चैतदवज्ञानं यत्सा कृष्णा सभां गता ॥८१॥
verses.english: And (when such is the case) Bhima and Arjuna can bring the very gods to the end of their life. This insult, namely that Krishna was dragged to the Assembly-Hall was offered to them;

verses.sanskrit: दुःशासनश्च कर्णश्च परुषाण्यभ्यभाषताम्। दुर्योधनो भीमसेनमभ्यगच्छन्मनस्विनम् ॥८२॥
पश्यतां कुरु‌मुख्यानां तस्य द्रक्ष्यति यत्फलम्। न हि वैरं समासाद्य प्रशाम्यति वृकोदरः ॥८३॥
verses.english: In the presence of the chiefs among the Kurus he will see what the consequences of that will be. Vrikodara having once been made an enemy cannot make peace.

verses.sanskrit: सुचिरादपि भीमस्य न हि वैरं प्रशाम्यति। यावदन्तं न नयति शात्रवाञ्छत्रुकर्शनः ॥८४॥
verses.english: The feelings of revenge in Bhima too will not calm down in a short time until that grinder of enemies does make an end of them.

verses.sanskrit: न दुःखं राज्यहरणं न च द्यूते पराजयः। प्रव्राजनं तु पुत्राणां न मे तद्दुःखकारणम् ॥८५॥
verses.english: The loss of kingdom is not a source of trouble, not even the defeat at the game of dice; nor even the exile of my sons was so much the cause of my affliction;

verses.sanskrit: यत्तु सा बृहती श्यामा एकवस्त्रा सभां गता। अशृणोत् परुषा वाचः किं नु दुःखतरं ततः ॥८६॥
verses.english: As that youthful Krishna, clothed in a single raiment brought into the Assembly Hall and that she was made to listen to harsh and insulting words, what can be more painful than that.

verses.sanskrit: स्त्रीधिर्मिणी वरारोहा क्षत्रधर्मरता सदा। नाभ्यगच्छत्तदा नाथं कृष्णा नाथवती सती ॥८७॥
यस्या मम सपुत्रायास्त्वं नाथो मधुसूदन। रामश्च बलिनां श्रेष्ठः प्रद्युम्नश्च महारथः ॥८८॥
verses.english: Having yourself, O slayer of Madhu, as the protector of myself with my sons and as also that foremost of powerful men, Rama and that great car-warrior Pradyumna; and having the invincible Bhima and Vijaya who never turn back from the field alive, that I should suffer this sort of grief, O best among men!

verses.sanskrit: साऽहमेवंविधं दुःखं सहेयं पुरुषोत्तम। भीमे जीवति दुर्धर्षे विजये चापलायिनि ॥८९॥

वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              तत आश्वासयामास पुत्राधिभिरभिप्लुताम्। पितृष्वसारं शोचन्तीं शौरिः पार्थसखः पृथाम् ॥९०॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Shauri, the friend of the Partha's, then comforted his paternal aunt Pritha who was lamenting being filled with grief on account of her sons.

verses.sanskrit:
वासुदेव उवाच।
              का तु सीमन्तिनी त्वादृक् लोकेष्वस्ति पितृष्वसः। शूरस्य राज्ञो दुहिता आजमीढकुलं गता ॥९१॥
verses.english: Vasudeva said O aunt, what woman is there in this world who is like you? The daughter of king Shura, you now (by marriage) a member of the Ajamida race.

verses.sanskrit: महाकुलीना भवती ह्रदाद्ध्रदमिवागता। ईश्वरी सर्वकल्याणी भर्त्रा परमपूजिता ॥९२॥
verses.english: Born in a noble family (and married to another equally noble family), you are (like a lotus) transplanted from one lake into another; you are the all-auspicious queen and much respected and beloved by your husband.

verses.sanskrit: वीरसूर्वीरपत्नी त्वं सर्वैः समुदिता गुणैः। सुखदुःखे महाप्राज्ञे त्वादृशी सोढुमर्हति ॥९३॥
verses.english: Yourself the wife of a hero, you have produced heroes; you are endued with all the virtues; it is fitting, of great wisdom as you are, that you should bear patiently happiness and misery like the Partha's.

verses.sanskrit: निद्रातन्द्रे क्रोधहर्षौ श्रुत्पिपासे हिमातपौ। एतानि पार्था निर्जित्य नित्यं वीरसुखे रताः ॥९४॥
verses.english: Sleep, laziness, anger, joy hunger and thirst, the Partha's having brought all these under control are ever attached to the enjoyment of happiness attainable by heroes only.

verses.sanskrit: त्यक्तग्राम्यसुखाः पार्था नित्यं वीरसुखप्रियाः। न तु स्वल्पेन तुष्येयुर्महोत्साहा महाबलाः ॥९५॥
verses.english: The Partha's ever desirous of enjoyment of heroes' life forego mean happiness; those men of great energy and great prowess were not content with a little.

verses.sanskrit: अन्तं धीरा निषेवन्ते मध्यं ग्राम्यसुखप्रियाः। उत्तमांश्च परिक्लेशान् भोगांश्चातीव मानुषान् ॥९६॥
verses.english: Those who are wise enjoy or suffer the extremes of whatever is enjoyable or sufferable. But person attached to mean happiness chose indifferent state of dullness; the former delight in the acutest sufferings or highest enjoyments; they do not like a middle course. They consider the extreme to be happiness, while that which lies between, is held by them to be misery.

verses.sanskrit: अन्तेषु रेमिरे धीरा न ते मध्येषु रेमिरे। अन्तप्राप्तिं सुखामाहुर्दुःखमन्तरमेतयोः ॥९७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: अन्तं राज्यं वा वनं वा मध्यमल्पैश्वर्यम् । अन्तपदं व्याचष्टे - उत्तमानिति । उत्तमान् तीव्रवैराग्यजान् परिक्लेशान् शीतवातादीन् ॥९६॥

verses.sanskrit: अभिवादयन्ति भवतीं पाण्डवाः सह कृष्णया। आत्मानं च कुशलिनं निवेद्याहुरनामयम् ॥९८॥
verses.english: The son of Pandu along with Krishna send their greetings to you; and having submitted to your notice that they are in health, asked about welfare.
verses.bhavadeepa: अन्तेषु अन्तयोः परब्रह्मानन्दे सुषुप्तौ वा उभयत्रैव द्वैतादर्शनात् सुखमस्ति एतयोरन्तरं जाग्रत्स्वप्नौ दुःखं दुःखरूपं स्वयमात्मा निर्दुःख एव जाग्रत्स्वप्नयोस्तूपाधिसम्बन्धात्तत्र भासमानं दुःखम् आगमापायित्वात्तत्र पुत्राः सहन्ते त्वं च सहस्वेति भावः ॥९७॥

verses.sanskrit: अरोगान् सर्वसिद्धार्थान् क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि पाण्डवान्। ईश्वरान् सर्वलोकस्य हतामित्रान् श्रियावृतान् ॥९९॥
verses.english: You will soon see the sons of Pandu without any illness and all their objects gained, the lords of all the world, with their enemies killed and themselves surrounded by prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: एवमाश्वासिता कुन्ती प्रत्युवाच जनार्दनम्। पुत्रादिभिरभिध्वस्ता निगृह्याबुद्धिजं तमः ॥१००॥
verses.english: Kunti who was filled with grief for her sons, thus comforted, said again to Janardana after driving away the gloom of her mind due to ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: कुन्त्युवाच। यद्यत्तेषां महाबाहो पथ्यं स्यान्मधुसूदन। यथा यथा त्वं मन्येथाः कुर्याः कृष्ण तथा तथा ॥१०१॥
verses.english: Kunti said-Whatever, O you with long arms, is beneficial in opinion, O slayer of Madhu and whatever you think right to be done, O Krishna, should be done.

verses.sanskrit: अविलोपेन धर्मस्य अनिकृत्या परंतप। प्रभावज्ञाऽस्मि ते कृष्ण सत्यस्याभिजनस्य च ॥१०२॥
verses.english: O chastiser of enemies let these be done without transgressing virtue and without the practice of deceit; I know, O Krishna, the power of your truth and your birth.

verses.sanskrit: व्यवस्थायां च मित्रेषु बुद्धिविक्रमयोस्तथा। त्वमेव नः कुले धर्मस्त्वं सत्यं त्वं तपो महत् ॥१०३॥
verses.english: And I know the wisdom and prowess you apply to the accomplishment of your decisions in any matter regarding your friends. In our family you are virtue, you are truth and you are the great devotee.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं त्राता त्वं महद्ब्रह्म त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। यथैवात्थ तथैवैतत्त्वयि सत्यं भविष्यति ॥१०४॥
verses.english: You are the saviour, you are the great Brahma, everything depends on you; what you have must come to pass for truth itself depends on you.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              तामामन्त्र्य च गोविन्दः कृत्वा चाभिप्रदक्षिणम्। प्रातिष्ठत महाबाहुर्दुर्योधनगृहान् प्रति ॥१०५॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Govinda of long arms bidding adieu to her and also going round her, went towards the residence if Duryodhana.
